verdict.rationale: Skyvern can be driven programmatically without its UI. It offers Python/TypeScript SDKs and a REST API, authenticated by API key, that run tasks in a cloud browser and return structured output. It can be self-hosted with pip, Docker Compose or Kubernetes, and a run can POST its result to a webhook when it finishes, which suits unattended automation. Missing for 10: explicit CI/CD integration docs (e.g. GitHub Actions or pipeline examples), explicit headless-mode documentation for self-hosted browsers, and independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Drive a cloud browser from Python or TypeScript with AI actions and Playwright, or run tasks and agents through the REST API.
You send Skyvern a prompt and a URL, Skyvern runs a cloud browser, and you get structured output back.
Run the Skyvern server on your own machine or cluster with pip, Docker Compose, or Kubernetes, using your own LLM keys or a local model.
Pass webhook_url when you start a run. Skyvern sends one POST to that URL when the run reaches a terminal status
Run end-to-end browser tests that adapt when the UI changes.
